tagline: Where rent was paid in apple trees.
intro: SR 39 and its side roads run between Mansfield and Loudonville, by way of Lucas, Mifflin and Perrysville, through the Mohican River country where John Chapman kept many of his nurseries. He reached the Mansfield area in the summer of 1809, just as the first town lots went on sale, and bought one.
Out here rent could be paid in trees. In 1826 John Oliver leased Chapman half an acre just west of Loudonville to plant fruit on, and the payment was 20 apple trees.

moments.title: Mansfield Square
moments.text: On the evening of August 10, 1813, Chapman is believed to have set out from here overnight to Clinton and Mount Vernon for help, returning the next day with reinforcements.

moments.title: Appleseed Landholding of 1814
moments.text: Half a mile southwest of the SR 39 and I-71 interchange, a wooded hill marks the quarter section Chapman leased with the widow Jane Cunningham, the first known of his many such leases.

moments.title: Copus Monument
moments.text: The obelisk raised in 1882 over Reverend James Copus and the militiamen killed defending his family in 1812 carries Chapman's name on its north side, the oldest known monument to mention him.
